title: Ruler Worship and the Imperial Cult
lead: From the kings who followed Alexander to the Roman emperors, rulers in the ancient world were honored as gods, with temples, priests, festivals and titles such as "Savior" and "Son of God." Jews and Christians who refused felt the pressure: under Antiochus IV (2 Maccabees 6:7), when crowds hailed Herod Agrippa as a god (Acts 12:22), in the charge that Christians said "Jesus is another king" (Acts 17:7), and in Revelation's beast and its image (Revelation 13).
